court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Bhagwan S/O. Kisan Janjal vs Anita W/O. Bhagwan Janjal And Others

parties.respondent_defendant: Anita W/O. Bhagwan Janjal And Others (wife and children)

facts_of_case: Petitioner is the husband of respondent No.1, who filed a maintenance application under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Petitioner also filed a divorce petition, which was pending before the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division). Respondent No.1 was already getting interim alimony as directed in the Hindu Marriage Petition.

legal_principles.principle: A proceeding initiated under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. cannot be stayed unless the petitioner expresses willingness to pay interim maintenance to all beneficiaries.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, unless the petitioner expresses his willingness to pay some interim maintenance to respondent Nos. 2 and 3, the proceeding initiated by them under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. cannot be stayed.

legal_principles.principle: A court may allow a proceeding initiated under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. to be decided finally, taking into account maintenance awarded under other statutes.
legal_principles.held: No prejudice would be caused to the petitioner if such a course is followed.
cited_cases: Ravindra Haribhau Karmarkar Vs. Mrs. Shaila Ravindra Karmarkar, (1992) Cri.L.J. 1845
Vijaykumar Gundappa Shetkar Vs. Bhagyawati Shetkar

outcome.final_order: The matter is heard finally at the stage of admission, and the proceeding under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. ought to have been stayed.
